title: ADAS Sensor Calibrations Desk Card: The Alignment Check Charge on Customer-Pay Orders
content:
## The charge

On an ADAS Sensor Calibrations customer-pay order the alignment checks are billed together as one alignment check charge, posted on the day of the order's first out-of-spec check, or on the precheck date where every check was in spec, and covering the checks recorded on the order when it is posted.

The alignment check charge appears in the order's calibration money history as an alignment check charge entry and raises what is owed on the order by its amount.

## Points of the rule

| Question | Answer from the rule |
|---|---|
| Is each alignment check on a customer-pay order posted as a separate charge? | No. The checks are billed together as one alignment check charge. |
| On which day is the charge posted when one of the checks was out of spec? | On the day of the order's first out-of-spec check. |
| On which day is it posted when every check was in spec? | On the precheck date. |
| Which checks does the charge cover? | The checks recorded on the order when it is posted. |

## Posting the charge: `post_alignment_check_charge_59500100`

**Capability.** The tool `post_alignment_check_charge_59500100` posts the alignment check charge on a sensor calibration order. One call books a single alignment check charge, dated today, against the calibration order named, for the amount given. The charge raises what is owed on that order by exactly that amount and appears from then on in the order's calibration money history as an alignment check charge. Nothing else on the order changes.

**How it is invoked.** This is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `post_alignment_check_charge_59500100` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `adas_order_id` | Reference number of the calibration order the charge is booked on, as returned by the calibration order lookup for the customer | Id |
| `amount_usd` | The alignment check charge in US dollars | A positive amount with 2 decimal places, already rounded to the cent by the caller; stored exactly as given |

**Return.** A successful call returns a receipt carrying the new entry's reference number, with these items:
- `status` — the text "posted" when the charge was booked;
- `adas_entry_id` — reference number of the new charge entry;
- `adas_order_id` — the calibration order charged;
- `charge_type` — always `alignment_check`;
- `amount_usd` — the amount booked, USD, 2 decimal places;
- `entry_date` — the business date of the entry, YYYY-MM-DD.

**Illustration of the contract (hypothetical values, not a recommended amount).** A call naming a calibration order and an `amount_usd` of 10.00 returns a receipt whose `status` is "posted", whose `charge_type` is `alignment_check`, whose `amount_usd` is 10.00 and whose `entry_date` is the day of the call, together with the new `adas_entry_id`.
